subject.title: [Bug]: Extension plugins silently skipped by gateway loader in v5.3+ (loads in CLI process, not in long-running daemon)

question: Should OpenClaw restore legacy startup loading for explicitly enabled external hook plugins that lack hook activation metadata, provided explicit deny and startup opt-out still win?
rationale: The central bug is source-proven, but the repair widens when local native plugin code executes inside the Gateway daemon, which is a security-boundary choice maintainers should confirm before landing the linked PR.

options.title: Restore legacy enabled-hook startup
options.body: Treat explicitly enabled non-bundled hook plugins as startup candidates while preserving deny rules, allowlist behavior, and `activation.onStartup: false`; this best matches the shipped compatibility regression.

options.title: Require activation metadata only
options.body: Keep the current strict rule and solve the user problem through docs, doctor diagnostics, and migration guidance, accepting that older security-hook plugins need manifest updates.

options.title: Split runtime fix from diagnostics
options.body: Land diagnostics or docs first and require a separate security-reviewed runtime PR for enabled-only legacy hook startup compatibility.

recommendation.title: Restore legacy enabled-hook startup
recommendation.body: Treat explicitly enabled non-bundled hook plugins as startup candidates while preserving deny rules, allowlist behavior, and `activation.onStartup: false`; this best matches the shipped compatibility regression.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin startup metadata unification makes this person the best available routing owner for the startup-planner/security-boundary choice.
